thread:
Alex G: Heads-up — noticed a weird path where a viewer saw the edit button in console for one customer. quick dump: user session was viewer, but UI showed editor affordance.
Mira S: ack. any repro steps? is this the migration cohort we rolled last night?
Alex G: yes, subset of customers migrated to the new role-mapping table. repro on prod for cust 'acme-inc' — clicking edit fails with permission denied, but button is visible.
Samir K: likely stale client-side cache or role matrix mismatch. can you grab the network trace / decoded token?
Alex G: pasted the relevant bits below:
```
GET /api/projects/1234/flags -> 200
user.roles: ["viewer"]
ui: renders Edit button if hasPerm(project_edit) // returns true clientside
server /authz/check -> 403
```
Mira S: interesting — server denies, client thinks allowed. where does client get hasPerm from? projection of role -> perms cached in localStorage for performance. we added short TTL for back-compat.
Jamie L: that cache key is populated on login and on push notifications for role changes. during the role-table migration we didn't emit the push for remapped roles. so client TTL kept older perms.
Samir K: that matches. but security question: can an attacker exploit this to perform edits? you said server returns 403 on action, so can't submit, but UI exposure is sensitive. potential social-engineering risk.
Alex G: agreed. also noticed audit logs for the click are sparse — no impersonation event or role-change metadata. need KMS-related audit correlation too.
Mira S: on audit logs — our KMS-encrypted audit blob doesn't include previous_role field right now. that's from the new role-mapping migration; we didn't add schema field.
Jamie L: timeline: migration job remapped role_alias -> canonical_role at midnight. we updated DB but forgot to push an audit-write update to include prev_role and mapping_source.
Samir K: OK concrete next steps (proposal):
1) Short-term UX fix: hide edit buttons if server-side /authz/check returns false, not rely solely on client cache. add a lightweight endpoint to fetch effective perms per route. (hotfix)
2) Mid-term: emit ws push after role remap or invalidate client perm cache via broadcast.
3) Audit schema: add prev_role and mapping_sha fields to audit payloads, and ensure they are KMS-encrypted and indexed in metadata for quick triage.
4) Postmortem + vulnerability check: run regen tests for UI gating across migration cohorts.
Mira S: +1. For 1) we can flip a feature flag to force server-verified gating in the console until rollout is complete. I'll open a quick flag.
Alex G: can someone check whether any active sessions had admin/editor perms leaked (i.e., client showed button and also an API token present that could be used from elsewhere)?
Samir K: scanned logs for last 8 hours: no accepted edit API calls from viewer tokens. found ~27 UI click events that returned 403. no successful privilege escalation.
sec-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: role-mapping-migration -> 2026-03-20T23:59Z had 0 push events emitted. See runbook /incidents/role-mapping-20260320.md
Jamie L: good to know. still need to tighten logs — the click events are recorded but missing tenant_prev_role which would speed root cause. I'll queue the audit schema change.
Mira S: KMS note: when we add prev_role into audit blob, ensure we don't break existing decrypt workflows — new field must be added to the latest envelope version and older readers should ignore unknown fields. update schema version header in envelope.
Samir K: also add a high-cardinality index on mapping_sha so we can quickly group affected tenants.
Alex G: action owners: Mira -> feature-flag hotfix and push invalidation; Jamie -> audit schema + KMS envelope bump; Samir -> search logs for related cohorts + write a short detection query to alert if client-visible affordance != server-permitted for any route; I'll draft the postmortem and coordinate comms.
Jamie L: ETA for hotfix? I can get flag flip and server gating in a PR today, deploy to canary, and roll to prod under the flag.
Mira S: I'll add the websocket push to the migration job, but safe to backfill with forced invalidation script run once across active sessions.
Samir K: detection query: `select count(*) from ui_clicks where route='project_edit' and server_status=403 group by tenant` — alert if > 5 in 1h. I'll own the alert.
Alex G: thanks. one more ask: we should add an audit test to the migration job that writes a sample audit entry and verifies decrypt + fields match. otherwise we keep missing these schema holes.
Jamie L: agreed. adding that to the migration pipeline now.
Mira S: I'll also update docs for frontend gating: never accept localStorage only for critical permission surfaces (edit/delete, billing, key management).
Alex G: perfect. thanks team — please update this thread with PR links and any unexpected findings. :thumbsup:
